newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Man from nowhere on hunger strike in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Man from nowhere on hunger strike in Cyprus.

text.p: A former Palestinian guerrilla on hunger strike in Cyprus on Friday vowed to stop only once a country is found willing to accept him.

Omar Hawillo, jailed for his part in a bungled 1988 attack on the Israeli embassy in Cyprus that killed three people, is on the seventh day of a hunger strike to publicise his search for a country willing to accept him now he is free.

"I came here from an Arab country and now they refuse to take me back. I don't have a country. My country is Block 10," Hawillo, 30, said in bitter reference to the detention cell he has been held in for the past 42 weeks.
Hawillo, who arrived in Cyprus on a forged Lebanese passport has been described as the man from nowhere -- no country, no nationality.

At the age of 22, he was jailed for 15 years for the Israeli embassy attack. He was released last August, but in accordance with Cypriot laws has been in detention since then pending his deportation to a country willing to accept him.

But none has been found to take Hawillo in, a fact diplomats attribute to their unwillingness to associate themselves with Hawillo and the faction he belonged to, although it was never actually clarified which one it was.
He started a hunger strike on June 6.

"I am not trying to blackmail anyone. I want my voice to reach humanity to help me," Hawillo, playing with worry beads with trembling hands, told Reuters in an interview in the police detention cells in Nicosia.
Police guards confirmed he has not touched food in days.
"I went to the United Nations. They judged me from my past and said they could not judge me a political refugee because of my criminal record."

But Hawillo says he has changed. "What I did at age 22 I regret deeply. It was wrong. I am not the one who blew up the car. I took part in the operation but now I have changed, I do not want to go back to that past."
The jeep rigged with explosives went off on a busy bridge after security personnel and police at the Israeli embassy twice prevented the driver from parking outside the building.
It was never clarified who detonated the bomb, which blew the Lebanese driver of the car, Hawillo's accomplice, to pieces. Two Cypriots passers-by were killed and 19 others injured.
Eight years behind bars have changed Hawillo from a timid youth to a confident, broad-shouldered man who has developed fluency in Greek and English and has learnt to work with computers.
But his skills have not helped him to start a new life.
"I've tried all the doors. Nobody cares."
